title: Mechanochemically tuned ZnO/ZIF-8 composites: evaluating the role of ZIF-8 in CO 2  electroreduction at high current density
content: ZIF-8 has attracted considerable interest for electrochemical CO2 reduction owing to its high CO2 adsorption capacity. However, whether enhanced CO2 adsorption translates into improved catalytic performance remains unclear. Here, we report a simple and sustainable mechanochemical route to systematically tune the conversion of commercial ZnO into ZIF-8 by varying only the grinding time. This approach enables the preparation of ZnO/ZIF-8 composites with controlled composition while minimizing solvent consumption. Increasing the grinding time from 1.5 to 12 h progressively increased the ZIF-8 fraction, specific surface area, and CO2 adsorption capacity, with CO2 uptake increasing from 0.96 to 1.77 mmol g−1 at 273 K and 100 kPa. Two composites containing 58% and 89% of ZIF-8 were evaluated for CO2 electroreduction in a zero-gap membrane electrode assembly at up to 300 mA cm−2. Although increasing the ZIF-8 fraction significantly improved CO2 adsorption, it did not improve catalytic performance. Instead, the composite with the lower ZIF-8 content consistently exhibited higher faradaic efficiency towards CO (76% to 57% from 50 to 300 mA cm−2) and lower cell voltages than the 89% ZIF-8 composite, while pristine ZnO outperformed both composites under the same conditions. These results show that CO2 adsorption alone is not a reliable predictor of electrochemical CO2 reduction performance under industrially relevant operating conditions and highlight mechanochemistry as a versatlile platform to systemetically control the composition of ZnO/ZIF-8 composites and examine the relationship between adsorption properties and electrocatalytic performance.
